stem: Alok knows the number of machines and the days to finish a fixed print job are inversely proportional. With $4$ machines the job takes $18$ days. He needs the time when $6$ machines work on the same job.

parts.text: Which claim correctly finds the time?

options.text: Keep the product constant: $4\times18=6\times t$, so $t=\dfrac{72}{6}=12$ days.
The constant product is only a label, so ignore the fixed job and pick any time.
Scale time the same way as machines: $t=18\times\dfrac{6}{4}=27$ days, as if the job size need not stay fixed.
The answer is $18$ days because $18$ is the only time printed in the stem.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Inverse proportion keeps the product fixed for the same job: 4×18=6×t gives t=12 days.

teacher.key_rationale: Inverse proportion keeps the product fixed: 4×18=6×t gives t=12. Treating 'constant product' as a mere label swaps the hinge. Direct scaling omits the fixed-job condition. Reusing the printed 18 is a surface grab.
